**Beta** from `{{REF}}` @ {{SHA}}: the next version, being tested before it becomes a stable release, so it can still change. For the stable version, take the latest release (not a beta). A server and its players need the same beta.

**New in 3.4.1 (beta):** **Find, name and travel to any Blood Altar:** the ruined altars scattered through Hell (a respawn anchor on crying obsidian among broken pillars, with a chest of offerings) and the altars players build are places now. Right-click one and it's remembered: it shows in your travel menu and on your Map of Hell (a purple mark), and stand beside it and type /rest name and then a name to name it (only you see it). If someone breaks it, it leaves your travel menu. **Three more guardians remade:** Cerberus is the Great Worm (three heads on long thick necks over a bloated, mangy body sagging into the mud), Plutus the wolf-headed banker (his belly turning to gold, his cloak sewn with coins, his rolling coin stamped with his wolf) and Phlegyas the drowned ferryman (weed in his beard, the sullen's chains across his chest, a huge black oar), all with new moves on the same timing. **Fixes:** travel sets you down beside a ruined altar, not inside its chest, and the Map of Hell's key no longer cuts its hints off on smaller screens. Before that, **3.4.0:** **Penitents on Purgatory:** each terrace now has souls working off their sin: the proud bowed under great stones, the envious huddled against the cliff, the wrathful walking in smoke, the slothful running round, the greedy lying in the dust, the gluttons standing under the fruit they can't reach, and the lustful walking through fire. They're scenery: they can't be hurt, keep off the stairs and only sigh (turn them off with the damnedSouls setting, like Hell's damned). **A lighter Map of Hell:** it keeps a small overview of everywhere you've been and loads the close-up pieces only as you zoom in, so a big explored world no longer eats memory or stutters when you open the map; zoomed in, the painted map of unexplored ground is sharp instead of blurry. **Every gatehouse tower has a door onto the wall:** in a few towers the stair blocked it; those now open on the far side, onto a walk along the wall top. **Lust's wind, twice as thick and different in every world:** a new world has 72 wind streams instead of 36, and where each one starts, how it bends and which way down it lands by are drawn from the world's seed, so no two worlds blow alike (worlds made before keep their first 36). **Name your Rests:** stand in a Virgil's Rest and type /rest name and then a name: it goes by that name in your travel menu, on your Map of Hell and in your Journal (only you see it; /rest name alone gives back its own name). Every Rest also has a clear name of its own now (its circle and its road, or its quarter for the four between the roads), so the travel menu no longer lists eight Rests per circle under the same name. **Small fixes:** Avarice's terrace floor is trodden earth instead of pale sand (it looked like snow), and Gluttony's water is a murky green so the puddles on its road show up. No new world needed, except for Lust's new wind (Purgatory's new floor shows where it hasn't been generated yet).

**From the 3.0 playtest:** the map is half as wide again (radius 5,250), so every circle is wider. **A shield blocks a boss's blow the moment it's raised**, so a late block on a white flash counts. Lust's **lovers** dive one pair at a time, and a dive blocked with a shield knocks them to the ground, stunned. Danger marks show over Cocytus's snow. The **roads** climb on stairs, some askew, with cracked and broken stones, and one circle's stone mixes into the next. **Lucifer is harder:** his fight runs faster and hits harder; the Fallen Seraph's wings turn most blows aside until you block his white slash (then he takes extra), and trading blows draws a riposte; the Emperor picks his blows at random, with little rest, and has new ones (both hands at once, a hand dragged round the ice, a frozen breath that sweeps a red wedge) while icicles keep falling. The climb out after him says plainly what is happening. Phlegyas swings his oar right round at arm's length (the purple ring is its reach), the Minotaur charges on both legs, and the bosses' and monsters' skins, fur and metal, and the blood armour's icons, are redrawn. **Every boss and monster has a new, more lifelike body** (faces with brows, noses and jaws, hands with fingers, wings of real feathers, layered clothes and armour; Cerberus bites forward, the centaurs aim their bows ahead, the harpies' wings beat the right way and the Malebranche keep their hooks in hand), and the Blood Heart and Tithe Axe have new icons. **The Wood of the Suicides is a thicket** now: gnarled trees with branches at head height and black thorns that slow you and tear you unless you sneak (sneaking is also what keeps the trees from screaming); the roads through it stay clear. **Angels fill Paradiso:** a host wheels round every sphere's island and a swarm flies in and out of the Celestial Rose, and the Angelic Guard are real angels now. **Make a new world.**

**New since phase 7 (Phase 8 so far):** ops can give anyone a testing kit with `/hellcraft loadout [players] [kit]` (works in single player with cheats on): the journey kits `upper`, `lower`, `lucifer` and `paradiso` give about what you'd have by then, hearts included (10, 12, 15, 18), to test the bosses fairly without the grind; `/hellcraft arena <boss> [lair] [players]` takes you to the edge of any boss's arena; `full` (the default) and `blood` give everything at once (maxed armour, every weapon, 16 ender pearls, 16 enchanted golden apples, totems). Every guardian of Hell now says something about Lucifer as it falls, and the Journal's Codex has a page on **the Emperor** that fills in, one piece for each guardian you beat. In boss fights your **style rank** now has its own panel on the right of the screen (the rank, a meter to the next one, and what just scored or cost you). Beat Minos, Cerberus, Plutus, Farinata or the Minotaur and its lair keeps a **lift** for you: stand in the soul fire in the middle for 3 seconds to go down to the next circle. The Foundry Halls' pillars have **chain-lifts** instead of ladders: stand on the plate by the chain to ride up to the arm, sneak to float down. In Paradiso, Beatrice gives the tips. **Every guardian of Hell now has four lairs** in its circle, one in each quarter of Hell (Phlegyas a landing by every watchtower, the Furies one inside every gate of Dis): fight it in whichever is nearest. There are **eight Virgil's Rests in every circle** now (four more between the roads, at the foot of a way down; Malebolge keeps four, its other bridges have the fake ones), and the travel menu has pages. **Make a new world** for the new lairs' level floors (in an old world they're built where the ground lies). The **relics** are real items now: the Halo is a gold circlet you wear, the Seraph Wings have white feathers, and Beatrice's Rose shows its hour's wait on the item.

**New in phase 7 (Purgatory and Paradiso):** **Purgatory** is its own world now, a mountain island in a starlit sea before dawn (the burrow and the climb out after Lucifer still take you there). **The Ascent** on its summit takes those who have beaten Lucifer up into **Paradiso**, also its own world: nine spheres of floating islands stacked one above the other, each with its own look, and the **Celestial Rose** in the Empyrean on top. In each sphere cross from the arrival isle to the great island, pass its short **trial** (gather the lights only you can see, against the clock on Mercury, catching them on Venus, in order on Jupiter's Eagle, up Jacob's Ladder on Saturn; beat the Angelic Guard on Mars), then stand in the **column of light** on the departure isle to rise to the next (hold sneak to sink back down). Falling can't hurt you there: angels catch you. The compass points the way. In the ninth sphere **the Seraph**, a six-winged angel on a real body, is the last trial (block its white wing-blow, run IN close for its Gloria, jump the turning heavens); beaten, it gives a **Halo**. Saturn gives **Seraph Wings**, the Rose's bell **Beatrice's Rose**. There are **no strongholds** any more (the End is vanilla and out of reach), and the Journal's second page tells the whole journey. **Make a new world.**

**Phase 6 (the Nether: the Forge of Dis):** the Nether is built from scratch round **the Great Forge**, Vulcan's smithy on a mesa at its centre (0, 0). Round the mesa lies **the Slag Sea**: cross it on the cooling crust, and keep moving, because it cracks under you and melts (four causeways of crust run straight to the stairs up the mesa). Beyond it lie four regions: **the Foundry Halls** (north: rivers of lava and great pillars with ladders), **the Chainlands** (east: islands hung on chains over the lava, joined by bridges), **the Ash Wastes** (south: piglins, bastions and fortresses) and **the Cyclops Quarries** (west: terraces with ramps, and the Cyclopes' camps). A column of heat rises over the Forge, and in the Nether the compass points to it. **Vulcan** fights on a real body now, with an entrance and the danger language (block his white hammer blow, jump his shockwave, step off his chain's red line; at half health the floor's seams burst). **The Cyclopes** are mini-bosses by their fires: block the maul, dodge the boulder, jump the stamp. **Make a new world.**

**Phase 5 (Lucifer):** Cocytus is cold: the cold builds while you're away from fire, so light the **braziers** on the ice (flint and steel or a torch); they stay lit for everyone. Every few minutes **Lucifer's wings beat** all over Hell, and from the Well of Giants you see them turning far off in the fog like a windmill. His pit is now a 70-block floor of ice. Step onto it and the fight starts in 30 seconds (sooner once everyone near is in), with a warning before the point of no return. **The Fallen Seraph** comes down in a cutscene and duels you in the danger language (block the white, dodge the red and purple); at half health he snaps and the traitors rise. Break him and **the mountain in the pit opens its eyes:** the Three-Faced Emperor, 10 times your height, who can only be hurt on the hands and faces he leaves down (block his bite to keep a face down longer) and whose wingbeat you hide from behind the six ice pillars. Beat him and you climb down his side and out to Purgatory. **From the Phase 4 play session:** the pit has no holes left to hide in, the lairs and Rests are spread out so each sits in its own circle, the roads are ruins with slab steps, Antaeus's arm swings the right way (and every boss's blows face forward), Geryon flies you a long way down, Lust has many more wind streams, and the ferry no longer drags you through blocks and lands you inside the Walls of Dis. **Make a new world.**

**Phase 4 (Lower Hell, Dis to the Giants):** each lower circle has a rule to play with. **Heresy:** the tombs blast fire in turn (watch the red circles and cross between blasts). **Phlegethon:** ford the river of blood at its shallows while the centaurs on the banks look away. **The Wood of the Suicides:** sneak, or the trees scream and call the harpies. **The Burning Sands:** fire falls in waves; shelter under the rock arches. **Malebolge:** nothing is what it seems: chests that breathe are mimics, a Rest that isn't on your compass is a trap, thieves snatch from your pack, and the Malebranche hook you along red lines (and their captain Malacoda will kindly show you a bridge). Five new guardians on real bodies: **the Furies** (who call **Medusa**: don't look at her while her eyes glow), **Farinata** in his burning tomb, **the Minotaur** and **Geryon**. Beat Geryon and he flies you down the great cliff; **Antaeus** sets you down on the ice of Cocytus from the Well. New monsters: heretics, centaurs, harpies, mimics, thieves and the Malebranche. **Make a new world** (the guardians' lairs and Antaeus moved). **From the Phase 4 play session:** the bosses fight at 60% of their old pace (longer wind-ups, warnings and parry windows; `bossTempo`), Geryon sinks low after each attack and the Furies land after their talons, so they can be hit, Lucifer hits for 70%, and more hearts help again (boss hits grow half as fast with them). The hell weapons and blood armour are real items now (and become infernal items at a Hellforge; old ones keep working). New: five enchantments found only in one circle each, among them **Sidestep** (leggings), which adds a **Dash** key (Left Alt) that dodges boss blows.

**Phase 3 (Upper Hell, Limbo to Wrath):** each upper circle has a rule to play with instead of a debuff. **Lust:** white wind streams carry you down the circle (step in; sneak to let go). **Gluttony:** the mud swallows whoever stands still (keep moving, or stand on roots, stone or planks). **Greed:** gold draws hoarders that steal it (stash it in an ender chest). **Wrath:** hands drag swimmers under where the Styx bubbles (keep to the roads, or take a boat). Limbo's **Noble Castle** stands on the east road, with shades who talk, trade and give Codex pages. New set-pieces in every circle (soul flocks over Lust, rotting trees and sunken feast tables in the Mire, coin hills, vaults and giant scales in Greed, fog, reeds, boardwalks and watchtowers in the Fen). **Cerberus, Plutus and Phlegyas** have real bodies and fights in the danger language; light the east watchtower's beacons to call Phlegyas, and any watchtower's to call his ferry to Dis. New monsters: the lovers, the gluttons, the hoarders and the wrathful. Fair play: no PvP in the Dark Wood, the Shore and Limbo, two hours of newcomer protection, and Cain's Mark for killing much weaker souls. **From the first play session:** what characters say now appears in a **dialogue box** above the hotbar instead of the chat; the Fen is lighter and its fog thinner; walking into Phlegyas's ring of braziers wakes him too; the older bosses no longer show the mob inside their model when hit by a potion effect; and the Spines over Cocytus are bent and broken instead of straight and mirrored. **Make a new world** for the new set-pieces and the new Spines.

**Phase 2 (boss tech, proven on Minos):** Minos has a real, animated body. Waking him plays a short cutscene (skippable once seen) with his name card. His fight speaks the danger language: **red** on the ground means get out, a **white** flash means raise your shield now (a block in time staggers him), **purple** can't be blocked, so jump it. Meeting him opens his entry in the Journal's Codex (J). The written guide book is gone: its pages are in the Journal.

**Phase 1, the new map:** Hell is 7,000 blocks across (border at 3,500). Four paved roads (east, south, west and north) lead from the Gate of Hell to the Well of Giants, and every cliff has a way down every 30 degrees. Entering a circle shows a card saying what it does and what to bring. A compass at the top of the screen points to the next way down and the nearest Virgil's Rest. **M** opens the Map of Hell and **J** the Pilgrim's Journal. **Make a new world:** worlds from older builds have the old map.

**Every player installs Hellcraft**, the same version as the server:
- **Modrinth App / Prism Launcher:** download `Hellcraft-{{VER}}-mc26.3.mrpack` and import it (it installs Minecraft 26.3, Fabric and Fabric API for you). Use it for single player and to join a Hellcraft server.
- **Official Minecraft Launcher:** download `hellcraft-{{VER}}-mc26.3-mods.zip` and follow `INSTALL.txt`.
- **Single player:** Create New World, World tab, World Type: **Inferno** (turn on *Allow Commands* for `/hellcraft goto <zone>`).

**Servers:** use `hellcraft-{{VER}}-mc26.3.jar` with the Docker setup in the README (`itzg/minecraft-server:java25`, `VERSION` 26.3). Only port 25565 is needed. Players without the matching Hellcraft are told what to install.
